sentence: This project images how metabolic activity varies inside head and neck tumors to learn why many patients do not respond to immune therapy.
This project builds an imaging tool that maps molecules in infectious disease by combining several kinds of image data.
This project follows people with HIV and people without it to study the genetics of the virus and how the immune system responds.
This project studies how myofibroblasts, the cells that make scar tissue, switch off after skin wound healing.
This project builds tools using machine learning that predict how patients with non-infectious uveitis respond to treatment and whether complications arise.
This project tries to find out which bacterial transcription factors turn on in the lung and let bacteria cause lasting infection.
This project studies the immune response to Clostridioides difficile, a toxin-producing bacterium, to help create vaccines that prevent infection.
This project matches research projects with the equipment and personnel available so that the equipment and personnel are used well.
This project uses machine learning to speed up the building and testing of red fluorescent calcium sensors that detect signals in neurons.
This project uses advisory groups to plan and check the progress of cancer research at a center.
This project collects, stores and shares human tissue and fluid specimens so that cancer researchers can use them.
This project studies the role of very-long-chain polyunsaturated fatty acids, lipids found in photoreceptors, in retinal health.
This project studies how prenatal stress shapes cellular risk of obesity and metabolic disease in infancy.
This project studies how rare genetic variants make T cells produce high amounts of inflammatory cytokines in juvenile idiopathic arthritis.
This project uses a mouse model to find out how the body keeps chronic myeloid leukemia under control after patients stop their medication.
This project sets up shared research services in a high containment lab for cell culture, microbiology, imaging and cell sorting.
This project looks for proteins on the surface of Clostridium difficile cells and spores to use as targets for mRNA vaccines.
This project studies how a kinase shapes signaling in pancreatic cancer cells and the immune cells around the tumor, using a mouse model.
This project studies the genetics of focal cortical dysplasia, a brain lesion linked to epilepsy, in a group of patients.
This project uses an animal model that regenerates well to test whether circadian rhythms affect regeneration by controlling cell proliferation.
